summary: @whalent/agent-core ships an obfuscated remote-controlled agent with PTY/SSH primitives and self-replacement channel
details: The package's declared `main` and `bin` entry point is a single 13 MB file (dist/index.cjs) heavily transformed with obfuscator.io: a rotated string array of ~103,000 entries, a custom decoder function, hex-named identifiers, and control-flow flattening. The bundle imports `node-pty` and `ssh2`, contains WebSocket client code with `onData` handlers, and references loopback remote-desktop ports (127.0.0.1:3389 for RDP and 127.0.0.1:5900/5901 for VNC). This is the shape of a remote-controlled agent that feeds network-sourced input into an interactive shell/PTY on the host running the bin. The README further documents that the package is 'replaced by remote daemon upgrades' — an out-of-band code-loading channel that bypasses the npm registry, allowing whoever controls the daemon endpoint to push arbitrary future code that then executes on the host at next run. The obfuscation hides the concrete network destinations and command grammar from installers and auditors. The combination — remote-driven PTY/SSH primitives, an author-controlled code-replacement channel, and deep obfuscation of the sole runtime file — matches a backdoor / remote-access-trojan pattern rather than a legitimate self-updating tool.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
